title: Minimum Support Price • 1 of 8
question: The Minimum Support Price (MSP) is a guaranteed price set by the Indian government to protect farmers from market fluctuations and ensure stable incomes while encouraging food production. After its introduction in the 60s, MSP has evolved into a key mechanism for income and food security, covering 23 essential commodities through the Food Corporation of India (FCI).

answers.text: It boosted food production and improved farmers' livelihoods while ensuring food security.
answers.message:
❌ Not quite!

While it secured farmer incomes, it also increased paddy cultivation so much that the government's rice stocks were way above the buffer stock norms, leading to massive inefficiencies. The MSP heavily incentivized farmers in Punjab and Haryana—regions with low rainfall—to cultivate paddy, which started a chain of events contributing to the infamous Delhi smog.

Markets and prices naturally guide production decisions. When interventions like the MSP attempt to override these signals through price controls, they often create long-term distortions that outweigh any short-term benefits.
